ev.q: Data from the 2019 national Youth Risk Behavior Survey were used to determine the prevalence of high school students’ self-reported experiences
Prevalence for each of these health risks was estimated by number of types of violence experiences.
Approximately one half of students (44.3%) experienced at least one type of violence
Female students (6.1%) were significantly more likely than were male students (3.4%) to experience three or more types of violence.
adjusting for sex, race/ethnicity, grade, and sexual identity
YRBS is a nationally representative, biennial, cross-sectional, complex school-based survey

methods_quotes.q: Logistic regression models with predicted marginals were used to quantify the associations between violence experiences
Pairwise comparisons were conducted using t-tests and considered significant if p<0.05.
Associations are presented as adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs).
Significantly different from zero types, based on linear contrast analysis (p<0.05).
Analyses were conducted using SAS callable SUDAAN (version 11.0.3; RTI International).
